findings.evidence: packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:518-524. When priorIdentity is undefined (epoch-0 close, no prior aggregate), a non-creator successor writer whose first creator-observed sequence exceeds one still throws LEGACY_MULTI_AUTHOR_MIGRATION_REQUIRED and aborts the whole close. The GREEN freeze paths at 528-546 are only reached for priorBoundary === null or numeric. That the shape is admissible is demonstrated by the f5a fixture itself: tests/fixtures/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5/foreign-author-close-liveness-contract.ts:208-226 routes a foreign authorSequence 2 vertex with no 0/1 present and it is admitted. The plan assigns only AUTHOR_REENTRY_PROOF_REQUIRED reachability to f5b (docs/production-hardening/production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md:98316-98319); the genesis-epoch legacy-migration variant of the same absent-prior branch is not named anywhere.
findings.impact: A first close of a two-writer room can be aborted permanently by an out-of-order foreign admission, which is the same liveness class f5a exists to remove. It is pre-existing, not introduced by GREEN, and it is fail closed rather than an authority defect, so it does not block this checkpoint.
findings.required_action: Add one sentence to the f5b prerequisite explicitly claiming the priorIdentity === undefined foreign branch (genesis-epoch legacy migration) alongside the author-reentry reachability question, so the residual is owned rather than implicit.
findings.title: Foreign-author close-liveness hole remains at a genesis close and has no named owner

findings.evidence: The plan states the anomalous row "must remain outside the issuance sequence range claimed by the aggregate frontier" (docs/production-hardening/production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md:98266-98269). The FOREIGN_REGRESSION treatment contradicts the letter of that sentence: tests/fixtures/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5/foreign-author-close-liveness-contract.ts:228-249 admits an epoch-1 foreign vertex at authorSequence 0 while the frozen boundary is 0, so the anomalous sequence is inside the claimed range. Safety actually holds because the range is identical to the authenticated prior and packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4750-4756 carries no per-sequence digest commitment (already documented as the accepted consumer contract at plan lines 97899-97902).
findings.impact: No behavioral defect today, but the plan's acceptance criterion does not describe what the retained test proves, and the fact that a creator-admitted current-epoch vertex can now share (author, sequence) with an already-covered historical row is an input f5b's settlement design must account for.
findings.required_action: Restate the f5a acceptance criterion as "the claimed range is exactly the authenticated prior and never advances through an anomalous row", and carry the shared-(author, sequence) case into the f5b audit's substitution obligations.
findings.title: Frozen-boundary safety argument rests on an unchanged range, not on the plan's stated exclusion

findings.evidence: .logs/d110c-0c1f5a-green-e379cfd2/validate.mjs:153-156 slices creator-close.ts between "async function authorIssuanceFrontiersCandidate(" and "async function successorAclCandidate(". No successorAclCandidate exists anywhere under packages/node/src, so indexOf returns -1 and slice(start, -1) yields the entire remainder of the file (inspectHead, persistSnapshot, stageCombinedGeneration, bindCreatorLiveClose).
findings.impact: The DUPLICATE_OWNER_MISSING, CREATOR_DUPLICATE_ERROR_MISSING, CREATOR_REGRESSION_ERROR_MISSING and FREEZE_PATH_MISSING invariants would pass on a match anywhere after that offset rather than inside the owner function. The conclusion is unaffected here because each searched string is unique in the file (I confirmed the owner directly at creator-close.ts:485-554) and OBSERVED_MAXIMUM_FORBIDDEN is only made stricter, but the validator does not enforce what it claims.

findings.evidence: docs/production-hardening/production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md:98278-98281 promises permutation of graph iteration, multiple simultaneous foreign anomalies, creator-plus-foreign anomaly precedence, permissionless writer-set derivation, creator deauthorization and remove/re-add with hidden history. The delivered contract covers the five cases, foreign removal/deauthorization and the two isolated creator controls only. I confirmed each absent item is currently redundant with the source shape (creator duplicate throws in the collection loop at creator-close.ts:489-495 regardless of iteration order; sequences are sorted numerically so byAuthor content is order-independent; each author's branch reads only its own sequences/priorBoundary/duplicateAuthors; the 64 bound is unit-tested at tests/protocol-v3-creator-author-issuance-frontiers.test.ts:212; writeAuthorizedAuthors is unchanged).
findings.impact: No untested defect today. The gap is that the single most security-relevant combination, a creator anomaly co-occurring with a foreign anomaly, is never exercised, so a later reordering of the duplicateAuthors freeze above the creator checks could silently reclassify creator corruption as author-local without any retained test failing.
findings.required_action: Add one creator-plus-foreign case (foreign duplicate present while the creator regresses) to the retained f5a contract asserting the exact creator error still aborts the close; the remaining items may stay recorded as redundant.
findings.title: Several promised adversarial matrix items are absent; guard ordering is structural but unpinned

findings.evidence: tests/fixtures/phase-6a-v3/creator-adoption-contract.ts:1141-1167 captures networkNode.gossipTopicFor into a local, installs the synthetic classifier, and restores the captured value in finally. All current callers await sequentially (contract line 60, adoption contract line 1243, repeat-close contract line 617), so the fix is correct as used.
findings.impact: If two routeRegisteredVertex calls ever overlap, the inner call captures and restores the synthetic classifier, leaving it permanently installed after both settle. That is exactly the poisoning failure this GREEN was written to remove, and it would resurface silently as a later direct-retained routing failure.
findings.required_action: When the fixture is next edited, guard installation with a depth counter or a shared install/restore owner so restoration is driven by the outermost caller rather than by each call's captured value.
findings.title: Shared fixture's gossip-classifier save/restore is not reentrancy-safe

summary: D.110c-0c1f5a is causally RED, closed by a genuinely narrow GREEN, and safe to close as this checkpoint. RED at 466169aa ran tests-only, exited 1, and its sole failure is the terminal token, which (each treatment throwing on any mismatch) proves all four foreign treatments plus both creator controls, the no-gap control, the same-close removal control and the currently-unauthorized snapshot refusal reached their exact pre-GREEN product errors on real signed/admitted vertices through the real close path. GREEN changes only per-author classification in authorIssuanceFrontiersCandidate(): creator duplicate still throws inside the collection loop before any per-author work (creator-close.ts:489-495), so creator-corruption precedence is structural and order-independent; creator regression/legacy still throw exactly (540-545, 532-537). Every foreign freeze pushes priorBoundary ?? null, so the emitted boundary can never exceed the authenticated prior. That is provably safe against the two consumers: creator-transition-advance.ts:441-444 rejects any proposed boundary below (or null under) a numeric prior, and v3-live.ts:4755 fails closed on a null admittedAuthorSequence, so no authority, replay, substitution or coverage widening is introduced; the anomalous vertex stays in the close set/history without advancing the frontier. The adjacent-prefix loop, minimum derivation, aggregate assembly order, signing, prepare/complete, and the protocol-v3 carrier are untouched (copiedFrontiers still enforces strictly increasing authors and the 64 bound), and successorAuthors ordering plus numeric sequence sort keep derivation deterministic. Tests prove the exact close-set count three ways (closeResult, cutValue.closeSetCount, and an independently rederived history closeOrder), the exact frozen/absent foreign entry, and a real verify -> commit -> activate -> issue -> publish adoption at epoch 2; the creator entry is proven transitively because inspectCreatorTransitionAdvance rejects any aggregate whose creator frontier differs from the retirement boundary. The shared fixture fix captures gossipTopicFor before install, installs inside try, and restores in finally after authenticated admission, and is proven by the D.109d baseline reproduction at the untouched RED anchor, the preserved early-restore timeout diagnostic, and the two-title boundary. Evidence is honest: the focused status-1 is attributed to the omitted coverage switch, failed intermediates are validated as failures, the 72-entry manifest is self-excluding, and the setup-only clean sibling is explicitly disclaimed. Scope holds: four files, no protocol-v3, wire, preimage, dependency, threshold, recovery-consumer or f5b settlement change. Five P2 debts recorded; none blocks closure.
